title: Aprepitant, A Neurokinin-1 Receptor Antagonist, as A Disruptive Drug for the Treatment of Pediatric Cancer
content: It is estimated that over 80% of children diagnosed with cancer will be cured. However, in recent years, the rate of improvement in the survival of children with cancer has slowed. Among the causes of death in pediatric cancer, the must be highlighted that due to chemoresistance of tumors and metastasis. In addition, with the increasing number of pediatric cancer survivors, the long-term severe side effects of chemotherapy have become increasingly evident. Thus, it is crucial to discover drugs with specific antitumor action, effective and safe that in combination with chemotherapy or radiotherapy have can chemosensitizer or radiosensitizer the tumor and decreased severe side effects of both. Substance P (SP) peptide and its Neurokinin-1 receptor (NK-1R) is known to be involved in pediatric cancer, promotion and progression. Pediatric cancer overexpresses SP and NK-1R, NK-1R which is essential for viability of cancer cells and is not essential for normal non tumor cells. SP is known to induce mitogenesis, have anti-apoptotic effects, SP induces angiogenesis, invasion and migration for metastasis in cancer cells and produces inflammation. In contrast, NK-1R antagonists, such as aprepitant and similar drugs, inhibit mitogenesis and induce apoptosis in pediatric cancer cells in a concentration-dependent manner. It also inhibits angiogenesis, invasion, and migration in pediatric cancer cells and has an anti-inflammatory effect. Moreover, aprepitant in combination with chemotherapy or radiotherapy can produces chemosensitization or radiosensitisation and decreases the severe side effects of both. This review updates the involvement of the SP/NK-1R system in pediatric cancer and the clinical application of NK-1R antagonist drugs such as aprepitant as a possible new drug for the treatment of pediatric cancer.
